Rajiv — great to hear. Happy to own the CS handoff and coordinate the kickoff. Proposed immediate next steps:
1) 30-min kickoff call to align scope and contact points (I can schedule Mon/Tue).
2) I'll share a mutual action plan (MAP) and an implementation checklist — Marissa will lead the CS-side execution, Evelyn will handle the technical runbook and schema alignment.

Quick answers:
- Max payload/tokens: we'll validate against your sample schema and propose a token window; typical recommendation for streaming assistants is to keep structured outputs under 2-4k tokens for consistent latency.
- Latency SLOs: we recommend 95th < 300ms for short responses; 99th depends on sequence length and batching — we'll propose concrete targets in the MAP.
- Auth for tool-calls: server-side preferred for initial rollout (safer), delegated OAuth for user-scoped calls later.
- Streaming + function-calls: supported, but you must ensure your function handlers can accept partial events or we buffer final calls — Evelyn will include patterns.

I'll attach the MAP and a shared Drive folder after this email. When is your engineering lead available for a 30-min window next Tue (16th) 10–12 PT?

Hi Rajiv / Connor — looping in the CS implementation runbook. I've sketched a pragmatic onboarding runbook below and attached an XLS MAP for signoff. Please review and flag anything missing.

Implementation Runbook (high level):
- Week 0 (Prep): access + networking
  - Provide API keys / environment names (dev, staging, prod)
  - Whitelist Redwood IPs for webhook callbacks OR configure outbound NAT
  - Confirm KMS/HSM policy if using private deployment
- Week 1 (PoC): streaming + simple tool-call
  - Enable streaming on the staging model route; test with 3 example prompts
  - Implement a single tool endpoint (POST /execute-triage) that returns JSON compliant with your sample schema
  - Validate schema using our schema-validator (we'll provide a containerized validator)
- Week 2 (Expand): structured outputs & robustness
  - Introduce stricter JSON schema (integration_schema_v2.json) and negative tests
  - Add retries, idempotency keys, and fallback path (non-structured text)
- Week 3 (Hardening): scale & SLOs
  - Perform load tests with streaming concurrency to observe 99th percentile latency
  - Tune batching and KV cache settings per workload (Evelyn will recommend defaults)

Pre-req checklist (what we need from MedLark):
- Example event payloads and max expected field sizes (your attached medlark_sample_schema_v1.json is great)
- Access to your staging environment + webhook endpoint
- Contact for security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence (if applicable)
- Confirmation on whether tool-calls will perform blocked IO (DB writes) or just read-only enrichment

Attachments: redwood_mutual_action_plan.xlsx, integration_schema_v2.json (draft)

Notes on streaming + function-calls:
- Best practice: stream token-by-token to your UI while postponing the final function invocation until the structured output is validated. If you need function-calls mid-stream, use a staged approach: partial events -> temporary buffer -> final call.
- Schema validation: we add a lightweight JSON schema validator as a pre-commit that runs in your CI for incoming tool outputs.

Next steps:
- Connor: schedule the kickoff (please include Eng and Security contacts)
- Rajiv: confirm Tue 16th 10–11 PT or propose alternatives
- Me: I will send the MAP for formal signoff today

Rajiv — quick technical responses and a recommended baseline configuration.

On Thu, Feb 18, 2026 at 14:45 Rajiv Menon <rajiv@medlark.com> wrote:
> 1) Payload/token sizing: our sample schema has a nested array of 50 items with descriptive text fields — worst case we expect ~6k tokens. Will that blow past your recommended window?

Short answer: 6k tokens is workable but will affect 99th percentile latency. Recommendation:
- Implement progressive chunking for the nested array: stream the assistant's top-level decision first, then paginated structured items in follow-up calls (or separate streaming chunks).
- Use a compact serialization for long descriptive fields (truncate or summarize in model prompt) so each item stays under ~200–300 tokens on average.

On Latency (99th < 600ms):
- For single short responses we can meet 99th < 300–400ms on hosted routes; for 6k-token structured outputs expect 99th to increase substantially (1–2s) depending on concurrency and batch window.
- Options to meet product target: dedicated route (reserved capacity) + tuned batching parameters + smaller KV cache miss rates. We'll propose a config in the MAP.

Security & onboarding packet:
- I'll attach a short checklist in the Drive: logs retained for 90 days by default (can extend for enterprise contracts), access via RBAC + audit logs, KMS integration supported for private deployments. Marissa will hand over SOC2 artifacts if needed.

Schema-validator container:
- Image: gcr.io/redwood-public/schema-validator:2026-02-10 (public read)
- CLI: runs as: docker run --rm gcr.io/redwood-public/schema-validator:2026-02-10 validate --schema integration_schema_v2.json --payload payload.json

Action items before kickoff:
- MedLark: confirm whether you prefer a single-call big JSON response or a paginated streaming approach (we recommend paginated for reliability).
- Connor/Marissa: lock in kickoff time and include SRE + security points of contact.

I'll prepare a short tech appendix with config snippets for streaming + function-calls together (including an example of buffering logic and idempotency keys).

Best,
